accepted_units.context_note: The introduction presents a periodic bipartite tiling as a compact joint representation: faces, edges, and vertices encode different parts of a quiver-style system, while a Kasteleyn construction recovers toric-diagram data. This is useful as a generic example of one combinatorial object coordinating several linked structures, but the identifications rely on the source's brane/quiver and dimer-model setting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the periodic tiling/quiver correspondence and Kasteleyn representation used by the source; the text does not supply a representation-independent proof, and its comparison of geometric and field-theoretic extremization is explicitly not general.
accepted_units.title: A periodic bipartite tiling compresses several linked structures
accepted_units.why_material: It illustrates a reusable conceptual move: seek a compact representation whose different cell types expose distinct semantic roles and whose algebraic invariant reconstructs another representation.

accepted_units.context_note: A toric Calabi--Yau cone is described successively by a moment-map cone with primitive facet normals, a lattice polytope obtained from the Calabi--Yau condition, a symplectic quotient, and a torus fibration whose homotopy sequence exposes topology of the link.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The equivalences use rational polyhedral toric geometry, a chosen lattice, smoothness assumptions, and the source's restriction to the simply connected three-complex-dimensional physical case; the orbifold extension is only indicated.
accepted_units.title: Move between cone, lattice, quotient, and fibration representations
accepted_units.why_material: This is a strong generic instance of geometricization: each representation makes a different invariant or computation visible, and the long exact sequence converts fibration data into lattice and homotopy information.

accepted_units.context_note: For adjacent toric normals, a determinant is related to the order of a Lens-space fundamental group and hence to torsion line bundles or flat connections. The source uses this topology to explain a multiplicity appearing in its physical construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The determinant and Lens-space topology are mathematical, but interpreting their cardinality as a field multiplicity depends on the source's distinguished-divisor and wrapped-brane conjectures.
accepted_units.title: Explain a combinatorial multiplicity through topology
accepted_units.why_material: It demonstrates a reusable explanatory bridge from an integer determinant to a finite fundamental group and then to a count of torsion geometric structures, while keeping the application-specific final interpretation explicit.

accepted_units.context_note: The quotient construction supplies line bundles whose first Chern classes and Poincare dual cycles are related by the same charge matrix used in the symplectic quotient. The source then interprets these cycle classes as baryonic charges.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The bundle, Chern-class, and Poincare-duality statements are geometric; their naming as field-theoretic charges depends on the AdS/CFT application and the stated fibration hypotheses.
accepted_units.title: Translate quotient relations into bundle and cycle classes
accepted_units.why_material: It shows how one relation matrix can be transported across quotient coordinates, line bundles, characteristic classes, and homology, revealing preserved structure under a change of mathematical language.

accepted_units.context_note: Flavor-charge representatives are constructed by lifting basis vectors through a quotient map. Two choices of lift differ by an element of the kernel lattice, which the source interprets as ambiguity from mixing with baryonic charges.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The quotient-and-lift ambiguity is generic lattice algebra; the labels flavor and baryonic, and the physical meaning assigned to the ambiguity, are application-specific.
accepted_units.title: Treat non-unique lifts as a controlled kernel ambiguity
accepted_units.why_material: This is a reusable move for parameter spaces and quotient objects: replace apparently arbitrary representatives by an explicit affine family modulo a kernel, then identify which quantities are invariant under that freedom.

accepted_units.context_note: The source formulates a geometric extremal problem in the Reeb-vector parameters that determines volume data from toric information without first constructing an explicit metric. It calls this the geometric analogue of a separate field-theoretic maximization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction assumes the toric Sasaki--Einstein setting and its admissible Reeb cone. The source does not prove general equivalence with field-theoretic a-maximization and later reiterates that limitation.
accepted_units.title: Replace an unavailable metric by a finite-dimensional extremal problem
accepted_units.why_material: It illustrates how geometric quantities can sometimes be inferred by optimizing over structural parameters rather than solving for a full object, a broadly useful compression provided the admissible domain and equivalence claims remain qualified.

accepted_units.context_note: Euler, charge, and R-charge constraints restrict possible tiling node types and their multiplicities but leave a one-parameter family rather than a unique combinatorial realization. The source associates the alternatives with different dual phases and notes additional non-generic phases.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The constraints are derived in the torus-tiling and supersymmetric gauge-theory model; the physical duality interpretation and completeness of the listed phases are not representation-independent conclusions.
accepted_units.title: Recognize when constraints define a family rather than a unique object
accepted_units.why_material: This gives a transferable diagnostic: solve global and local constraints, count the remaining degrees of freedom, and treat the residual parameter as meaningful structure instead of forcing uniqueness.

accepted_units.context_note: For the parameterized family, the source reduces a constrained cubic maximization to stationarity equations, compares those equations with a geometric system, and selects the admissible local maximum among formal critical solutions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The calculation is family-specific and embedded in physical charge constraints. Agreement of the reduced equations in this family is evidence, not a proof that the two extremization principles are generally equivalent.
accepted_units.title: Compare two extremal descriptions through reduced equations and admissibility
accepted_units.why_material: It supplies a conservative comparison strategy: reduce both descriptions to common variables, compare their defining equations, and separately check domain admissibility rather than identifying objectives merely from matching examples.

accepted_units.context_note: A brane tiling encodes a quiver and interactions, while local transformations on particular tiles change building-block counts but preserve boundary data and are used to relate different global phases. The text flags periodicity subtleties and treats non-generic phases separately.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact block shapes and gluing rules are figure-dependent, and the interpretation as Seiberg duality is physical. Boundary preservation and periodic compatibility must be checked in the represented tiling rather than inferred from the count update alone.
accepted_units.title: Use local representation moves to navigate a family of global realizations
accepted_units.why_material: It is a reusable pattern for moduli of representations: identify local moves, record their invariant boundary interface, and analyze how repeated moves connect distinct presentations without claiming literal equality of their internal descriptions.
